title: International Workers’ Day assembly in Tirana
scope: May Day assembly/march in Tirana; a separate reported action at the Marinza oilfield is treated as a separate excluded action, not combined.
organizer: Union of Trade Unions of Albania and Albanian Coalition for Labour Rights, as named in the CLR statement.
participants_original: CIVICUS and the CLR organizer statement describe hundreds of workers; no numeric count or range is given.
threshold_50_evidence: The contemporary organizer statement and CIVICUS report both use “hundreds,” supporting the threshold qualitatively; exact attendance and independent confirmation are unresolved.

start_date.summary: Both accounts date the Tirana gathering to 1 May 2025.

location.summary: Both place the assembly/march in Tirana; CLR locates it at Mother Teresa Square.

organizer.summary: CLR statement names the Union of Trade Unions of Albania and Albanian Coalition for Labour Rights as organizers.

demands.summary: Fair wages, safe working conditions, labor rights and related economic concerns; CLR also explicitly called on the government to begin dialogue with unions.

participants_original.summary: Both say hundreds; neither gives a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative “hundreds” supports >=50 without converting it into a numeric lower bound.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed accounts do not establish violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response is established in the reviewed passages; each response field remains unknown.

notes: CIVICUS S001 was read in April and directly links the CLR PDF; preserve this shared written-origin relationship, not independent corroboration. Citizens.al S002 is an issue/advance report, not execution evidence. No event-specific state response or violence was identified in reviewed passages.
open_questions: Can a numeric attendance estimate or independent contemporary account be found?
What was the event’s exact end time and did the government take any response?
Does any further evidence establish violence or its absence?

title: Opposition protest rejecting parliamentary election results
location: Tirana; precise venue not stated in the reviewed CIVICUS account.
scope: One opposition protest in Tirana against the 11 May parliamentary election results. The OSAC search-result title is a separate title-only demonstration lead near the U.S. Embassy; it has no body verification and is not merged with this event.
organizer: Democratic Party, led by Sali Berisha, according to CIVICUS.
participants_original: CIVICUS describes turnout as small; no count or range is supplied.
threshold_50_evidence: Unresolved. “Small” does not establish whether attendance reached 50; no numeric estimate was found in the reviewed account.

start_date.summary: CIVICUS explicitly dates the protest to 16 May 2025.

location.summary: CIVICUS places the protest in Tirana but gives no precise venue.

organizer.summary: CIVICUS says the demonstration was led by Democratic Party head Sali Berisha.

demands.summary: CIVICUS says the opposition protest rejected the results of the 11 May parliamentary election.

participants_original.summary: CIVICUS calls turnout small without a number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Attendance cannot be resolved against the 50-person threshold from the qualitative term alone.

protester_violence.summary: CIVICUS reports protesters and MPs verbally and physically assaulted journalists; this supports violence by participants, while responsibility across categories is not further separated.

state_response.summary: CIVICUS reports no major police intervention; it does not explicitly resolve any of the seven response dimensions, so all remain unknown.

notes: CIVICUS is a retrospective report published in June and is the only opened evidence for this event in this dossier. OSAC S007 is a title-only search lead for a planned demonstration near the U.S. Embassy on the same day; its body was not reviewed, its exact venue and execution are unknown, and no merge is made. The stated election-result demand is a political-process target, not an act of electoral support.
open_questions: What was the precise venue and event end date?
What event-specific state responses occurred beyond the report of no major intervention?
Does the OSAC title-only planned demonstration near the U.S. Embassy identify the same action or a separate event? Its exact venue and execution remain unverified.

title: Pride Parade 2025 in Tirana
location: Tirana; reported march from Reja through central streets to the Prime Minister’s Office.
scope: One annual Pride march in Tirana; exact duration and final dispersal time are unknown.
participants_original: Citizens.al and CIVICUS describe hundreds; no numeric estimate or range is given.
threshold_50_evidence: The two accounts use “hundreds,” supporting the threshold qualitatively; exact count and independence of reporting remain unresolved because CIVICUS links to Citizens.al.

start_date.summary: Both sources date the Pride Parade to 24 May 2025.

location.summary: Both place the march in Tirana; Citizens.al gives a route to the Prime Minister’s Office.

organizer.summary: The reviewed article identifies activists and supporters but does not name an organizing body.

demands.summary: Equality, safety, legal recognition of same-sex couples, and rights/protection for LGBTQI+ people.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Qualitative “hundreds” supports threshold; count and independent-source relationship remain open.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed passage does not establish violence or its absence.

state_response.summary: Health Minister Albana Koçiu attended and expressed support/invited dialogue; no formal agreement, concession, or other response field is established.

notes: CIVICUS S001 links to Citizens.al S005; treat as related reporting, not independent confirmation. A ministerial expression of support is reported but does not establish accommodation as defined here.
open_questions: Can an independent attendance estimate and named organizer be found?
What happened at the march’s end and what other event-specific state responses occurred?
Did any formal government accommodation follow the minister’s remarks?
